name: Cyera
summary: Cyera sells data-security software that finds and protects sensitive data across companies' cloud systems and AI tools.
overview: Cyera provides a data security platform that discovers sensitive data, controls who and what can access it, and governs how AI systems use it.
bull_case: As companies deploy AI on their own data, controlling what those systems can see becomes essential, and Cyera is an early leader.
bear_case: Large security platforms such as Microsoft, Palo Alto Networks and CrowdStrike can bundle similar features.

intelligence.description: Cyera provides a data security platform that discovers sensitive data, controls who and what can access it, and governs how AI systems use it.
company: Cyera was founded in 2021 by Yotam Segev and Tamar Bar-Ilan, veterans of Israeli military cyber units. Its platform maps where sensitive data lives across cloud and on-premises systems and controls access to it, and it now positions that as the trust layer for enterprise AI.

In June 2026 Cyera raised $600 million at a $12 billion valuation, led by Evolution Equity Partners with Temasek and existing backers including Accel, Blackstone and Coatue. The company says annual recurring revenue has tripled three years in a row, and it has made five acquisitions.
intelligence.why_it_matters: Cyera shows how AI adoption is creating new security spending around data access, and it is one of the fastest-rising private cybersecurity companies.

changed.text: Cyera is founded by Yotam Segev and Tamar Bar-Ilan.

takeaways: The valuation doubled in a year.
AI data governance is a new and fast-growing budget line.
Reported revenue multiples are high, so growth needs to continue.
